explainer_reply:
The highlighted tokens consistently appear in phrases that assign or introduce a name, title, or designation for something. The strongest activations fall on verbs like "called," "named," "entitled," and multiword expressions like "known as," "referred to as," and "by the name of," all of which precede a proper name or technical term. Weaker activations appear on related naming contexts: quotation marks or colons introducing a title, "call it" constructions, and even code keywords (class, TABLE) that declare a named entity.

[EXPLANATION]: Words and phrases used to introduce the name, title, or designation of a person, thing, or concept, such as "called," "named," "known as," "referred to as," and "entitled," typically appearing just before the name itself.
